title: Research paper
one_line_goal: Results analysed; paper drafted with every claim checked
summary: Turn the raw data from the campaigns into analysed results and a draft paper. Every number comes from scripts, every citation is verified, failed experiments are reported, and nothing is called new beyond what you approved. You read the whole paper as its responsible author.

tasks.title: Set up the paper project
tasks.what: The paper project: a LaTeX setup in the research folder with a build script, using the [proposed ACM template](ref:adr-0017) or its replacement.
tasks.why: A paper that builds from day one lets writing start at any time.
tasks.how: Claude installs the LaTeX tools and you click the admin prompt ([who installs](ref:adr-0021)); the skeleton must build a PDF with no errors, and the tool version is recorded.
tasks.chain: We need a paper that builds from day one → set up the LaTeX project with the [proposed ACM template](ref:adr-0017); Claude installs the tools and you click the admin prompt ([who installs](ref:adr-0021)) → writing can start any time.
tasks.check: The empty paper builds to a PDF with no errors; the tool version is recorded.

tasks.title: Analyse the campaigns
tasks.what: Analysis of both campaigns: averages, confidence ranges, effect sizes and corrections, with each prediction marked supported, not supported or inconclusive.
tasks.why: Raw data alone proves nothing; each verdict must rest on a repeatable analysis.
tasks.how: Run the statistics pipeline from the benchmark phase on the raw data, link each verdict to its output, and rerun from scratch to confirm identical results.
tasks.chain: Raw data alone proves nothing → run the statistics pipeline on all campaign data and mark each prediction supported, not supported or inconclusive → every verdict links to its analysis.
tasks.check: Every experiment is analysed; a rerun from raw data in a clean setup gives identical output.

tasks.title: Figures and numbers from scripts only
tasks.what: Every figure, table and number in the paper, made by scripts, with a record of which data and script made each.
tasks.why: Hand-typed numbers invite mistakes; generated ones are traceable.
tasks.how: Scripts write the figures and number files the paper reads in; a check script fails if the text contains a result number not from a generated file.
tasks.chain: Hand-typed numbers invite mistakes → every figure, table and number in the paper is generated by a script, with a record of which data made each → every number is traceable.
tasks.check: A check fails if the paper holds a result no script produced; every figure is in the record.

tasks.title: Trace from question to conclusion
tasks.what: A table linking each research question to its prediction, experiment, raw data, analysis, figure and conclusion, shown in this portal.
tasks.why: Each conclusion must rest on evidence, and gaps should be visible at a glance.
tasks.how: Generate the table from the wiki, and check that no reported conclusion has an empty cell.
tasks.chain: Each conclusion must rest on evidence → build a table linking question → prediction → experiment → raw data → analysis → figure → conclusion, shown in this portal → gaps are visible at a glance.
tasks.check: No empty cell for any reported conclusion; the wiki link checks are clean.

tasks.title: Write method and design sections
tasks.what: The paper's method, architecture, tab-sleeping design and background sections.
tasks.why: These parts do not depend on results, so the paper can move on without waiting for data.
tasks.how: Write them first, with every factual claim citing a wiki page, research note or reference; you review them.
tasks.chain: Method and design do not depend on results → write method, architecture, tab-sleeping design and background first → the paper moves on without waiting for data.
tasks.check: The sections build; every claim cites a source; you review them.

tasks.title: Write results and limitations
tasks.what: The results, security and usability trade-offs, and limitations sections, including energy limits, process counting, debugging-channel effects and the single PC.
tasks.why: Results must come only from finished analysis, so there are no early or unsupported claims.
tasks.how: Start only once each cited experiment is analysed, and make sure the limits cover every open risk and every unsupported measurement.
tasks.chain: Results must come only from finished analysis → after it, write results, security and usability trade-offs, and the limits (energy, process counting, debugging-channel effects, one PC) → no early or unsupported claims.
tasks.check: Every experiment cited in results is analysed; the limits cover every open risk and unsupported measurement.

tasks.title: Related work, introduction, abstract
tasks.what: The related-work section, then the introduction and abstract, written last.
tasks.why: Claims of novelty must match the approved literature check, so the paper never overclaims.
tasks.how: Write related work from the closed literature check, then map every novelty sentence to the approved assessment; you sign off.
tasks.chain: Claims of novelty must match the approved literature check → write related work from it, then the introduction and abstract last → the paper never overclaims.
tasks.check: Each novelty sentence maps to the approved check; you sign off.

tasks.title: Verify every citation
tasks.what: A check of every reference in the paper against its actual source or its permanent paper ID (DOI).
tasks.why: A wrong or made-up citation damages trust in the whole paper.
tasks.how: A script resolves every paper ID, each reference has a research note, and nothing from the 'do not cite' list is used; its output is saved.
tasks.chain: A wrong citation damages trust → a script confirms each reference against its source or its permanent paper ID (DOI) → no unverified or banned references.
tasks.check: The citation check shows zero unresolved entries and none from the do-not-cite list.

tasks.title: Report failed experiments too
tasks.what: A record, in the paper or its appendix, of every failed or stopped experiment run.
tasks.why: Hiding failures is cherry-picking; reporting them keeps the record honest.
tasks.how: Go through the project log and run records and mention every aborted or failed run.
tasks.chain: Hiding failures is cherry-picking → list every failed or stopped run from the log and run records in the paper or its appendix → the record is honest.
tasks.check: Every failed or stopped run is mentioned in the paper or its appendix.

tasks.title: Reproducibility package
tasks.what: The reproducibility package: final reproduction guide, scripts, setup records, the data (or an archive with checksums) and a licence for the data.
tasks.why: Others must be able to check our work and rebuild every figure.
tasks.how: Do a dry run on a fresh copy of the project that rebuilds all figures from the archived raw data, and save its output.
tasks.chain: Others must be able to check our work → package the guide, scripts, setup records and data (or an archive with checksums) with a data licence → anyone can rebuild every figure.
tasks.check: A fresh copy rebuilds all figures from the archived data; the output is saved.

tasks.title: AI-use statement
tasks.what: The final statement of how AI helped, matching the chosen venue's policy, with the human authors' responsibility.
tasks.why: Venues require honest disclosure of AI help, and humans stay responsible for the claims.
tasks.how: Finish the AI-use document to match the chosen venue's policy; you review and approve it.
tasks.chain: Venues require disclosure of AI help → finish the AI-use statement to match the chosen venue's policy, with the human authors' responsibility → honest and compliant.

tasks.title: Integrity check and your review
tasks.what: The end-of-phase integrity check and your review of the whole paper.
tasks.why: Nothing invented may go out: no made-up facts, versions, measurements, citations or novelty.
tasks.how: Complete and save the integrity checklist, run the wiki check, then you read the paper as its responsible author and approve the end of this phase.
tasks.chain: The paper is drafted → a checklist confirms no invented facts, versions, measurements, citations or novelty → you read the paper and approve the end of P8.
tasks.check: The checklist is saved, the wiki check is clean, and you approve the end of P8.

test_gate.explanation: Analysis tests pass and a rerun gives identical output → the paper builds → every number comes from a script → every citation checks out → every conclusion traces to data → you read the whole paper and approve.

rows.proves: The analysis code passes its tests.
Rerunning the analysis gives byte-identical results.
The manuscript compiles to a PDF without errors.
No result in the paper was typed by hand.
Every reference is verified; none is banned.
Every conclusion links back to its raw data.
The plan pages are consistent and have no broken links.
You stand behind every claim as a human author.
You checked the limitations and the failed experiments.
You approved the AI-use statement and the reproduction guide.
